hints.title: Self Join Interval Overlap
hints.text: Join meetings with itself on same employee and date where meeting IDs differ.

hints.title: Time Interval Condition
hints.text: Two intervals overlap if the start time of each is strictly before the end time of the other.

hints.title: Distinct Overlapping Meetings
hints.text: Tally unique meeting occurrences involved in conflicts and join employee information.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH overlapping_pairs AS (
    SELECT 
        m1.employee_id,
        m1.meeting_date,
        COUNT(DISTINCT m1.meeting_id) AS overlapping_meetings_count
    FROM meetings m1
    JOIN meetings m2 ON m1.employee_id = m2.employee_id 
                    AND m1.meeting_date = m2.meeting_date 
                    AND m1.meeting_id != m2.meeting_id
                    AND m1.start_time < m2.end_time 
                    AND m2.start_time < m1.end_time
    GROUP BY m1.employee_id, m1.meeting_date
)
SELECT 
    e.employee_id,
    e.employee_name,
    e.department,
    o.meeting_date,
    o.overlapping_meetings_count
FROM overlapping_pairs o
JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id
ORDER BY o.meeting_date ASC, e.employee_id ASC;
```

variables: M: meeting records per employee day
complexity.notes: Self join on employee day partitions with interval overlap predicates.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all pairs across different dates or employees creates unpartitioned quadratic overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Filtering by employee and date restricts self-joins to small daily buckets.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use self-join with start1 < end2 AND start2 < end1 condition.

import pandas as pd

def find_overbooked_employees(employees: pd.DataFrame, meetings: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    m = meetings.merge(meetings, on=['employee_id', 'meeting_date'], suffixes=('_1', '_2'))
    m = m[m['meeting_id_1'] != m['meeting_id_2']]
    overlaps = m[(m['start_time_1'] < m['end_time_2']) & (m['start_time_2'] < m['end_time_1'])]
    
    grouped = overlaps.groupby(['employee_id', 'meeting_date'])['meeting_id_1'].nunique().reset_index(name='overlapping_meetings_count')
    res = grouped.merge(employees, on='employee_id', how='inner')
    res = res.sort_values(by=['meeting_date', 'employee_id'], ascending=[True, True])
    return res[['employee_id', 'employee_name', 'department', 'meeting_date', 'overlapping_meetings_count']]
